room_or_space: Whole-building transverse section (sheet label reads SECTION); no room or level names are given on the sheet

proportions.notable_proportion: No dimensions or scale are written, so only relative proportions as drawn can be read: three stacked levels of which the partly sunken lower level is drawn roughly 1.4x taller (floor to floor) than either the main or the upper level, which are about equal; the three terraces step out progressively to the left (upper balcony shortest, main-level balcony about twice as long, grade-level terrace longest), so that the composition with terraces is roughly 1.5x the width of the main building body; the main body (excluding terraces) is wider than it is tall, about 1.3:1 from lower floor to roof, and the roof overhang on the left projects well beyond the upper-level wall line

layout.organisation: Three stacked levels: a partly sunken lower level, a main level and an upper level under a low-pitched roof with a deep overhang. Each level is bounded on the left by a cantilevered terrace or balcony enclosed by a brick parapet, the terraces lengthening from top to bottom. The main body is closed on the right by a tall, solid masonry wall that rises above the roof and is capped; a second brick masonry mass (chimney) rises through the roof left of centre. The upper level is subdivided into three rooms (two small on the left, one larger on the right); the main level and lower level each show a smaller left-hand space and a larger right-hand space divided by a full-height partition.
layout.axes: Strongly horizontal: floor and roof slabs, terrace slabs and the copings of the brick parapets read as continuous horizontal bands stepping outward to the left; the low roof and its tapered soffit reinforce this. Vertical counterpoint comes only from the two masonry masses (the chimney through the roof and the capped right-hand end wall) and from the slender full-height glazed openings between terraces and interiors.
layout.entry_sequence: No front door, porch or stair is drawn. The only exterior-to-interior transitions shown are on the left, one per level: grade terrace to lower level, main-level balcony to main level, upper balcony to upper level, each through a narrow full-height glazed opening behind a brick parapet.
layout.circulation: No stairs or vertical circulation between the three levels are shown. Internal movement is indicated only by doorways with dropped heads (lintel notches) in partitions: one between the two small upper-level rooms, two in the large upper-level room (one at its left partition, one near the right exterior wall), and one in a partition at the lower level. Door leaves are drawn in elevation on the far walls of the two small upper-level rooms.
